issues: The diff changes only TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE (2**19 to 2**18). It does not touch the evaluation call, the metric, the data, the seed lines or the summary printing, so there is no integrity concern.

No bug makes the result meaningless. Assuming the usual seq len of 2048, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 gives 131072 tokens per micro-step, so 2**18 still divides evenly (grad accumulation 2 instead of 4). If it didn't divide evenly, the run would have failed its assertion rather than given a silently wrong number.
Candidate mean is 1.06275 and the incumbent is 1.1026, a difference of 0.03985. The incumbent has only 1 run, so its variance can't be estimated from these numbers.

z = 6.166 can't be reproduced exactly. It implies a noise sd of 0.03985/6.166 ≈ 0.00646, which presumably comes from a harness-wide noise estimate. Using only the candidate spread (sd ≈ 0.00488) gives z ≈ 8.2 against a single-run sd, or ≈ 11.5 against the standard error of the mean. Every way of computing it gives at least 6.17, so 'accept' is consistent with the numbers.

Note: the incumbent's mean is based on 1 run. Smaller batches mean more optimizer steps within the fixed 300 s, so a gain is plausible. A replicate run of the incumbent would make the comparison firmer, but it isn't required.
